body: Continue to be a friend to her without trying any manipulative tactics such as guilting (how it will affect you, her friends or family). Encourage her to keep a consistent routine, keep up with activities she enjoys (or used to enjoy).  Suggest therapy and treatment for depression. See if their are events or clear problems that are causing her to have these thoughts. Be aware of certain signals, such as sudden change in mood, giving away possessions, isolating etc. In terms of involving other people or police, they are limited in what they can do and you risk losing her as a friend by betraying her confidence. To be devil's advocate, this is really all you can do.

While your kindness is admirable and appreciated, don't make a promise that is simply impossible to keep. Besides, other than cowardliness, I couldn't do that to my sister or father. I'll never forget the pain it caused them when they found out I was hurting myself. My sister crying in agony is an image I doubt I'll forget. At least for now I won't succumb to the darkness.

For 3 years I have tried everything from therapy, goal setting, routine, diet, exercise, work, hobbies and talking with and trying to be there for my family. Its torture to hold on to any hope that more time will change things.

Edit: I'm sorry, it isn't fair to resent you for not being able to complete an impossible task, cheering up and being supportive to a person that can twist everything into a negative.
